faqs.a: Not exactly. Disposition none means the receiver took no action (usually because your policy is p=none). A message can have disposition none and still fail DMARC. The DKIM and SPF columns tell you whether authentication actually passed.

faqs.a: Aggregate reports are daily summaries: counts per IP with pass/fail results, but no message content. Forensic (ruf) reports are per-message samples with redacted headers. This tool reads aggregate reports, which is what most rua= mailboxes receive.
faqs.q: What is the difference between aggregate and forensic reports?

faqs.a: Reports cover roughly the previous 24 hours and arrive once a day per provider. Google and Microsoft are usually prompt; smaller providers may skip days. If you published your record less than 48 hours ago, wait a little longer.
faqs.q: How fresh is the data in a report?

dmarc-xml-report-analyzer.formula:
pass_rate = (messages with disposition=none AND dkim=pass AND spf=pass) / total_messages x 100
acted_on = messages with disposition=quarantine OR disposition=reject
unique_ips = distinct source_ip values across all records
howTo: Copy the full XML from a DMARC aggregate report (the attachment in your rua= mailbox).
Paste it into the box above. The report parses instantly — nothing is uploaded.
Read the summary: total messages, pass rate, messages acted on, and unique sending IPs.
Scan the records table, sorted by volume. Focus on rows where DKIM or SPF failed.
For failing rows from services you use, fix authentication (SPF include or DKIM signing). For unknown failing IPs, investigate before trusting them.
keyFacts: DMARC aggregate reports are XML files sent daily to your rua= address by mailbox providers (Google, Microsoft, Yahoo and others).
Each <record> in the report describes one sending IP: how many messages it sent and whether DKIM/SPF passed and what the receiver did.
<policy_evaluated> holds the verdict: disposition (none, quarantine, reject) plus the dkim and spf results.
<auth_results> shows the details: which DKIM domain and selector were checked, and which SPF domain was evaluated.
The report also carries <report_metadata> (who sent it, which day it covers) and <policy_published> (the DMARC policy the receiver saw).
A high pass rate with disposition none means your mail authenticates fine — you are ready to move from p=none toward enforcement.

dmarc-xml-report-analyzer.workedExample:
Sample report from google.com covering one 24-hour window, policy p=reject:
Record 1: IP 203.0.113.7, 42 messages, disposition none, DKIM pass, SPF pass.
Record 2: IP 198.51.100.23, 5 messages, disposition reject, DKIM fail, SPF fail.
Summary computed by the tool:
1. Total messages: 42 + 5 = 47.
2. Fully authenticated: 42 (only record 1 has disposition none with both checks passing).
3. Pass rate: 42 / 47 x 100 = 89.4%.
4. Acted on: 5 messages rejected.
5. Unique sending IPs: 2.
Reading: the 5 rejected messages from an unknown IP failed both checks — likely spoofing, correctly blocked.
